_notes: 3510-3639: All feast-day title strings from the sanctoral calendar. No scripture verses; no WebFetch needed. Notes on specific entries: (1) 'S. Felicis II' — Felix II is traditionally listed as martyr, though historically disputed; translated as殉道者 per breviary usage. (2) 'S. Ioachim' appears twice (3565 with doubled O.N. form, 3566 as standalone) — both translated identically. (3) 3565 vs 3566 differ only in that 3565 has a doubled line (standard + O.N.), 3566 is the standalone form. (4) 'S. Iohn Baptist Rossi Confessor' (3587) and 'S. Iohn I, pope and martyr' (3588) are English-language strings in the Latin data — translated as if titles, using Catholic names. (5) 'S. Iuan Diego' (3597) — the indigenous Mexican saint; 圣胡安·迪耶戈 is the standard Catholic Chinese rendering. (6) 'S. Iosaphat' — Josaphat Kuntsevych, Bishop and Martyr; 约沙法特 is the 思高/Catholic form. (7) 'S. Ioannis Baptistæ de la Salle' and 'de Rossi' — these are both St. John the Baptist (patron name) forms, not the same person as John the Baptist; rendered with 若翰 (Baptist's name form) to distinguish from St. John the Apostle/Evangelist (若望). (8) 'S. Gregorii Thaumaturgi' — 大奇迹家 is the standard Catholic Chinese epithet for Gregory the Wonderworker. (9) 'S. Hormisdæ II' — the 'II' appears unusual; Pope Hormisdas was the first of that name; translated as listed per the breviary text without correction. (10) 'Gregorio Barbadico' — Gregory Barbarigo, Bishop of Padua, canonized 1960; 巴尔巴里戈 is the standard transliteration. (11) 'S. Iustini' — Justin Martyr; 贾斯汀 is a common Catholic Chinese rendering; some sources use 犹斯定. (12) 'S. Iuvenalis' — Juvenal of Narni; 若弗纳利 is a provisional transliteration; flagged as uncertain. (13) 'S. Fridolini' — Fridolin of Säckingen; 弗里多林 is a provisional transliteration. (14) 'S. Gulielmi' — William (of Vercelli or Bourges); 威廉 is standard. (15) 'Brundusium' = Brindisi (Italian city); 布林迪西 is standard.
